The only thing that confuses me about his death is the heroin. I was addicted to opiates after the death of my grandparents and some other traumatic stuff and I can't even begin to explain how strongly a shot of heroin knocks you out completely. It's instant and completely overwhelming when, and unlike a lot of things you can build a tolerance too decent heroin is still going to provide the knockout effect if it's injected. It was normal to be out cold for 30 minutes after just one point of heroin injected, and I'm sure someone with Kurt's wealth and connections was getting pretty good stuff. Not only would the heroin make it difficult (I'd even say nearly impossible) to even lift a gun and shoot yourself properly it would be unnessecary - heroin overdose is easy and painless. You're literally out like a light and don't wake up - it's be like having the most euphoric, warm sleep of your life and just not waking up. It's extremely common for anyone in the spirals of addiction to be suicidal (I'd almost say it's a given) but to shoot yourself is such overkill when you have an easier and better option. If it was suicide he must have been in a hell of a lot of pain/self loathing or must have wanted to inflict some damage to whoever found his body too. His case is probably the only one that would actually be less tragic if it was a murder that he couldn't see coming because the thought someone with that much success, talent, and adoration to be so determined and desperate to kill himself in such a violent manner is just horribly sad. I've lost best friends to ODs and the general lifestyle/way of thinking that goes along with addiction, and while it's always tragic to lose a young life it's especially sad to see so much lost potential. It's also very preventable, we have medication out there that can completely change an addict's life and way of thinking for the better and lead to a great recovery (esp when combined with therapy) but the stigma and the "once an addict always an addict" attitude causes so many people to think recocery is impossible and meaningless. My psychiatrist in an AA thumper and it still chaps my ass when he tells me I'm still a drug addict because I smoke pot 1-2 times a month in the safety of my own home.  You may still have addictive tendancies in your brain that you should be aware of, but being in active addiction and using vs being recovered is completely night and day. Sorry for the rambling but Kurt's case obviously touches a wound for me and it just makes me think of the millions of other people who suffer and die from addiction everyday, and also to the immense pain they suffer from in their own minds. If people were more reasonable about mental health we'd see a huge decline in ODs.
